summary:
[  edit  ]
NOTE
License:  Only available in  TouchDesigner Pro .
The  Sync In CHOP  and  Sync Out CHOP  are used to keep timelines in two or more TouchDesigner processes within a single frame of each other. One process will contain a  Sync Out CHOP  while one or more other processes contain  Sync In CHOPs . The processes with  Sync In CHOPs  should have their  Realtime flag checked off , as their frame rates will be determined by the  Sync Out CHOP .  Also note, all monitors (including all clients and server) should be set to the  same rate .  Note that unplugging or re-adding monitors may sometime change previously configured settings.
The CHOPs synchronize by pausing their own timeline until all Sync In/Out CHOPs have cooked. The  Sync Out CHOP  will be ahead of the  Sync In CHOPs . If any CHOPs fail to communicate, the others will timeout, causing all processes to run slowly.
Client machines may come online at any point, or be switched off as desired, as the  Sync Out CHOP  will adjust accordingly, either timing out, temporarily or permanently banning individual clients as specified.
In addition any extra  CHOP  channels sent through the  Sync Out CHOP  is received by the  Sync In CHOPs .
NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues make sure Windows Firewall is disabled.
An  Info DAT , pointing to the  Sync Out CHOP , provides a detailed list of all clients:
The columns are:
pid : process id of the client
address : ip and port number
machine_name : client machine name
filename : name of the   .toe   file the client resides in
op_path : full operator path to the client
include :  when 1, the Sync Out CHOPs waits for a reply, when 0, it is ignored.
timeout_total :  The total number of times the Sync Out  CHOP  stalled waiting for this client
timeout_consecutive :  The running number of times the Sync Out  CHOP  stalled waiting for this client.
steady_total : The total number of times the Sync Out  CHOP  received a reply in time.
steady_consecutive : The running number of times the Sync Out  CHOP  received a reply in time:
reply :  The last reply from the client, all clients should have the same increasing value.
Similarly, an  Info CHOP  will reveal further information:  Info CHOP Channels
Example Files   [  edit  ]
Here are two simple example files that use Sync In and Out CHOPs. You would run the SyncServer .toe  only once, and run the SyncClient .toe  for every machine you want to display on. Note that you may need to adjust the  Window COMP  located at /perform to output to your desired monitor. Also note that  Hardware Frame Lock  is not enabled in these examples, so if you want to use that feature you'll need to turn that parameter on in the  Window COMP  for SyncClient .toe  as well.
File:SyncServer.toe
File:SyncClient.toe
Intermittent Connections   [  edit  ]
Whenever a client replies, it is immediately assumed reliable, and waited upon, by the  Sync Out CHOP  each frame thereafter.
When a client times-out a number of times in a row, however, it is continuously ignored by the  Sync Out CHOP , until it replies on time again.
This also applies to clients that have stopped communicating altogether.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Whether or not the  CHOP  is currently attempting to synchronize itself.

parameters.label: Multicast Address
parameters.name: multicastaddress
parameters.description: An IP address to communicate on (224.0.0.1).

parameters.label: Network Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The network port associated with the address.

parameters.label: Local Address
parameters.name: localaddress
parameters.description: Specify an IP address to send from, useful when the system has mulitple NICs (Network Interface Card) and you want to select which one to use.

parameters.label: Local Port Mode
parameters.name: localportmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose between automatically or manually selecting local port to use.

parameters.label: Local Port
parameters.name: localport
parameters.description: When the above parameter is set to 'Manual', enter the port number to use here.

parameters.label: Timeout (msec)
parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: The maximum amount of time the  CHOP  will wait for synchronization signals from the other Sync CHOPs. This value is expressed in milliseconds.

parameters.label: Client Timeouts (Consecutive)
parameters.name: clienttimeouts
parameters.description: The maximum number of consecutive timeouts a client must generate until it is ignored, causing no further timeouts. It will remain ignored until it replies on time again or this  CHOP  is reset.

parameters.label: Ban Clients
parameters.name: banclients
parameters.description: Enables permanent banning of clients.

parameters.label: Total Timeouts
parameters.name: banclienttimeouts
parameters.description: The maximum number of timeouts a client must generate until it is permanently ignored. Only a reset will allow it to be included again.

parameters.label: Clear Stats
parameters.name: clearstats
parameters.description: Pressing this button will clear all banned lists, as well as totals reported in an  Info CHOP .

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.label: Channel Names:  c[1
parameters.description: 10:2] ambient

parameters.label: Rename To:  b[1
parameters.description: 5] amb    This example fetches channels  c1 c3 c5 c7 c9  and  ambient .

parameters.label: sync_incompletes
parameters.description: This number is constant when the system is in sync, and will climb up each time the number of clients responding does not match the expected number.  When all is steady, the number does not change .

parameters.label: sync_totaldelay
parameters.description: The total amount of time spent waiting for acknowledgement replies from the clients (milliseconds).

parameters.label: sync_lastdelay
parameters.description: The amount of time waiting for acknowledgement replies from the clients for the last message (milliseconds).

parameters.label: sync_internal
parameters.description: The number of clients within the same  .toe  file (process) that it is waiting on.

parameters.label: sync_external
parameters.description: The number of clients from different  .toe  files (other processes) that it is waiting on.

parameters.label: sync_serial
parameters.description: The last serial index sent to the clients. Increases each message sent.

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
